findings.title: Compile error: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments
Passkeys no longer set up on the initial login form when no user is set
Test try/catch swallows the assertion failure

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Compile error: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47-47

Explanation:
The second commit changed the signature to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. `UsernameForm` still calls the no-argument form, so the module will not compile. The condition should be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. Since `context.getUser() != null` is already checked first, passing the user also makes the helper's own `user != null` check redundant.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) {
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Passkeys no longer set up on the initial login form when no user is set

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:114-117
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:137-140
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162

Explanation:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` returns false when `user == null`. In the regular first-visit login, the user is null, so `fillContextForm` is never called. That removes conditional UI and passkey login from the main login page, which is the primary use case. The previous code explicitly handled `user == null`. The helper should not require a non-null user. The same applies to the error `challenge` path. It also breaks `UsernameForm`, where the user is null on first display.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() {
    return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled();
}
// callers: if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Missing `@Override` on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64-67

Explanation:
The method overrides a protected method of the parent class but lacks `@Override`, so a signature mismatch would not be caught by the compiler. Add `@Override`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
@Override
protected boolean shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext context) { return false; }
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Test try/catch swallows the assertion failure

Affected:
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:291-296
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:312-317

Explanation:
`catch (Exception)` does not catch `AssertionError`, so that part is fine. However, `fail(...)` throws `AssertionError`, which is an `Error`, so it propagates correctly. The real problem is that the pattern is convoluted: `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` and the `nullValue()` assertion is never reached. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` or `findElements(...).isEmpty()` instead.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
Assert.assertTrue(driver.findElements(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")).isEmpty());
~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Compile error: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the signature was changed to require a UserModel parameter
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies exactly the same problem as the golden comment: the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() method is being called without arguments in UsernameForm, but the method signature requires a UserModel parameter. Both comments point to the same bug - a method call missing a required parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
